title.description: The product title, for the listing's `title`. Format: 'Brand Primary Product Keyword | Product Type / Material | Key Feature | Primary Application / Use Case | Variant Specification', using ' | ' as the delimiter. 120-150 characters — do not exceed 150. The brand is `house_brand` from the get_product result, the same name that goes in `brand`; when there is none the title carries no brand at all and opens with the product keyword. The highest-volume search keyword goes immediately after the brand, and a brand, when there is one, appears ONCE, at the start. Include variant specifications (Color, Size, Capacity, Dimensions, Pack Size, Material, Pattern, Style, Model) only when they are explicitly provided; where they are not, expand using product features and intended applications rather than inventing a spec. Every child variant gets a unique title from its own specifications. Readable, not keyword-stuffed. No emojis, no ALL CAPS, no promotional or restricted words, no seller name, phone number, website or price.

bullet_points.description: EXACTLY five bullet points, for the listing's `bullet_points` table, in this fixed order: (1) Material / Construction, (2) Design, (3) Multipurpose Applications, (4) Capacity / Functionality, (5) Everyday Use. Each is an UPPERCASE feature heading, then ' - ', then the description — e.g. 'LARGE CAPACITY - Main compartment fits A4 documents, laptop up to 14 inches, and daily essentials'. Aim for 180-250 characters each. Work high-volume Amazon search keywords in naturally, never repeating a keyword or feature across bullets. Plain text, professional and easy to read. Include variant specifications only when explicitly provided.

description.description: The product description, for the listing's `description`. 180-250 words of plain text (no HTML, no markdown), in four paragraphs — (1) Product Overview using the primary product keyword, (2) Material & Features, (3) Applications & Use Cases, (4) Everyday Use — followed by a summary block on its own lines: 'Package Includes:', 'Material:', 'Color:', 'Size:', 'Dimensions:', 'Capacity:', 'Usage:'. Include ONLY the summary fields the product information actually provides; omit the rest of the lines entirely. Never invent, assume or infer a specification. No exaggeration and no unsupported performance claims.

keywords.description: Amazon BACKEND search terms, for the listing's `keywords` table — invisible to the shopper. Put here only the terms that did NOT earn a place in the title or bullets: synonyms, alternate and regional spellings, common misspellings, and related use cases. Never repeat a word that already appears in the title or bullets; Amazon already indexes those and a repeat wastes the byte budget. No competitor brand names, no third-party IP, no ASINs, no subjective claims ('best', 'cheapest'), no temporary statements ('new', 'sale'). Keep the whole set under roughly 250 bytes. Reuse a keyword from get_reference_values verbatim when it applies, so the catalog stays consistent.

images.description: Images produced by the image step, for the listing's `images` table, in the order the tool returned them — copy its result entries VERBATIM, including each entry's `role`. The first entry is always the main image (role 'main'); the rest are the gallery in order. An empty array when no image step ran, when the product has no photos, or when the per-request image toggle was off.

role.description: 'main' for the image Amazon shows in search results — the variant's own photo, on a plain white background. 'gallery' for the remaining family images, in order. Copied verbatim from the image step's result entry; never decided by you.

kind.description: What was done to this image, in the image step's own vocabulary (e.g. 'white-background', 'translated').

source_url.description: The input photo this image was derived from, when there was one.

url.description: The resulting image, or null. Null is the normal case: the image step queues the work and it is rendered in the background after this run finishes, then attached to the listing. Copy null through as-is — it does not mean the image failed, and it does not belong in needs_review.

note.description: What the image step said about this entry, copied verbatim when it gave one. Leave null otherwise; do not write your own explanation of a null url.

needs_review.description: Human-readable names of fields that could NOT be confidently filled and must be completed by the admin before publish (e.g. 'Material', 'Bullet 5', 'Search Terms', 'Main image background').

confidence.description: Overall confidence in the enrichment given the quality of the source data and photos.

brand.description: The house brand this product sells under, copied character for character from `house_brand` in the get_product result. You do not decide this and you do not change it -- it is classified against the seller's own brand descriptions before the enrichment starts, and the title opens with the same name. null ONLY when get_product returned no `house_brand`, meaning this deployment has no house brands or the classification could not be made; then the title carries no brand either. Never a brand read off the incoming listing title. Never derived from the product's category or Item Group. If you believe the classification is wrong, use it anyway and say why in `notes`.

notes.description: Anything the admin should know: assumptions made, ambiguities, which of the listing's Amazon issues this enrichment addresses, which it cannot (pricing, inventory, category approval, compliance), what substantiates any otherwise-restricted claim you used, or conflicts between the product text and the photos.
